source.citation: Ramsey M, Vaughton G, Peakall R (2006). Does inbreeding avoidance maintain gender dimorphism in Wurmbea dioica (Colchicaceae)? Journal of Evolutionary Biology 19:1497-1506.
source.table: Table 2, p.1500; methods pp.1499-1501; Figure 2 and results p.1502
source.access: Full primary-article text mirror, checked against publisher abstract; original family records unavailable
source.population: YY, southeastern Australian Wurmbea dioica ssp. dioica
source.data_level: Published rounded treatment means and standard errors; manual factual transcription

measurement_semantics.seed_unit: seeds per maternal plant, published treatment mean
measurement_semantics.germination_condition: seed germination among sampled mature seeds, monitored for four months
measurement_semantics.survival_condition: survival of planted germinated seedlings through the second growing season
measurement_semantics.corm_mass_unit: mg per surviving offspring, growth proxy
measurement_semantics.index_definition: Successive products of treatment means, then ratio between groups; not the mean of family-specific products

sampling.note: Different stage-specific family sets; no single common sample size or within-family covariance is available

author_reported.interpretation: Reported point estimates are retained separately from Table 2 arithmetic; no correction to the original paper is asserted

claim_limits: The 2006 fruiting males were already female-functional at collection; their prior male-only expression histories are unknown
No linkage to the 1999 tagged transition cohort or the 2012 resource-induced cohort
Open controls were pollinated in the field before excavation; self/cross treatments were pollinated in a glasshouse; crossed fruiting males were emasculated
Treatment contrasts are among different maternal plants; no paired genotype crossover or complete isolation of the effect of selfing
Corm mass is a growth proxy, not observed adult reproduction, paternal success, or lifetime fitness
Products of marginal means are descriptive indices; family selection and unobserved covariance prevent inference of exact cohort totals
No new sampling confidence intervals or significance tests can be reconstructed from the published marginal SEs alone
Printed-mean rounding bounds are deterministic sensitivity bounds, not sampling uncertainty
Marker outcrossing rates were measured among germinated seedlings, not zygotes; no further multiplication by cumulative inbreeding depression
The 1.4 abstract summary matches the seed-number ratio, while the four-component crossed female/male index is about 1.25; the original results also report reciprocal cumulative RP about 0.80
The original-text Mo/Mc cumulative 0.23 is not reproduced by the transcribed table means; do not pool, replace, or silently reconcile it with the derived 0.296
